translationRepairs: In the fourth year of the Daming era of Song (460), he was nominated as Outstanding Talent. His elder brother Sao was also well known and had already taken the provincial nomination in an earlier year. The Vice Prefect Wang Yuanceng of Donghai then wrote to Huan's father Hui: "In recent years your worthy sons have filled the quota of Outstanding Talent; the province and its people may truly be said to have found the right men."

In the fourth year of the Daming era of Song (460), he was nominated as Outstanding Talent. His elder brother Sui was also well known and had already taken the provincial nomination in an earlier year. The Vice Prefect Wang Yuanceng of Donghai then wrote to Huan's father Hui: "In recent years your worthy sons have filled the quota of Outstanding Talent; the province and its people may truly be said to have found the right men."
The given name is 璲, read Suí; Sao is a romanization error, and Sui is the accurate English form.

In the fourth year of Daming of Song, he was nominated as Outstanding Talent. His elder brother Sao was also renowned and had earlier responded to the provincial nomination. At this time the Vice Prefect Wang Yuanceng of Donghai wrote to Huan's father Hui: "In recent years your worthy sons have filled the quota of Outstanding Talent; the province and community may be said to have found the right men."

In the fourth year of Daming of Song, he was nominated as Outstanding Talent. His elder brother Sui was also renowned and had earlier responded to the provincial nomination. At this time the Vice Prefect Wang Yuanceng of Donghai wrote to Huan's father Hui: "In recent years your worthy sons have filled the quota of Outstanding Talent; the province and community may be said to have found the right men."
The literal likewise wrongly renders 璲 as Sao; Sui matches the Chinese given name.
The emperor wished to appoint Huan Secretariat Gentleman and had Minister of Officials He Jian convey his intent.
The emperor wished to appoint Huan as Secretariat Gentleman and had Minister of Officials He Ji convey his intent.
戢 is jí, so 何戢 is He Ji, not He Jian. Adding as before the office is grammatical and does not change the sense of 用瓛爲中書郎.
The Emperor wished to employ Huan as Secretariat Gentleman and had the Minister of the Ministry of Officials He Jian convey his intent.
The Emperor wished to employ Huan as Secretariat Gentleman and had the Minister of the Ministry of Officials He Ji convey his intent.
The literal repeats the same misreading of 何戢 as He Jian; He Ji is required.

Jian said to Huan: "His Majesty wishes to place you in the Secretariat—the Phoenix Pool—but regrets that your seniority is still slight. You may accept the previous appointment for the moment; in a few days you will be transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and the higher post will follow immediately thereafter."

Ji said to Huan: "His Majesty wishes to place you in the Secretariat—the Phoenix Pool—but regrets that your seniority is still slight. You may accept the previous appointment for the moment; in a few days you will be transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and the higher post will follow immediately thereafter."
The speaker is named 戢; the shortened English given name must be Ji, not Jian.

Jian said to Huan: "His Majesty wishes to place you in the Phoenix Pool; he regrets that your qualifications are light. You may for the moment accept the previous appointment; in a few days you will be transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and then the later post will be conferred at once."

Ji said to Huan: "His Majesty wishes to place you in the Phoenix Pool; he regrets that your qualifications are light. You may for the moment accept the previous appointment; in a few days you will be transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and then the later post will be conferred at once."
The literal attribution 戢謂瓛曰 likewise requires Ji rather than Jian.
The courtesy name is 子璥 (Zǐjǐng). Zijun does not match 璥; Zijing is the correct romanization.
Before he could move in he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to conduct the fast at Huan's house.
Before he could move in he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to take Ye to conduct the fast at Huan's house.
將曅 is omitted from the English. 將 is the verb take/lead and 曅 is a personal name, so restoring take Ye is required by the Chinese.
The literal 字子璥 must be Zijing, not Zijun; 璥 is jǐng.
Before he could move his residence he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to lead the fast at Huan's house.
Before he could move his residence he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to take Ye to lead the fast at Huan's house.
The literal also drops 將曅. Taking Ye to lead the fast at Huan's house restores the omitted name and the verb 將.

At the beginning of the Taishi era of Song, he served as Palace Attendant in the Masters of Writing; in deliberations on the empress's taboo name and those outside the palace, all followed the old practice of using surnames.

At the beginning of the Taishi era of Song, he served as Gentleman of the Palace Hall in the Masters of Writing; in deliberations on the empress's taboo name and those outside the palace, all followed the old practice of using surnames.
尚書殿中郎 is a gentleman of the palace hall in the Masters of Writing, not 侍中 Palace Attendant.

At the beginning of Taishi of Song, he became Palace Attendant in the Masters of Writing; in discussing the taboo name of the empress and those outside the palace, all followed the old practice of using surnames.

At the beginning of Taishi of Song, he became Gentleman of the Palace Hall in the Masters of Writing; in discussing the taboo name of the empress and those outside the palace, all followed the old practice of using surnames.
The literal has the same office error: 殿中郎 is Gentleman of the Palace Hall, not Palace Attendant.

Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's argument that the empress does not use her surname, and that in the Spring and Autumn Annals the queen was moved against to Qi. Cheng failed to cite clear classical evidence and instead based his position on personal opinion; for this he was dismissed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.

Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's argument that the empress does not use her surname, and that in the Spring and Autumn Annals the queen was met and escorted from Qi. Cheng failed to cite clear classical evidence and instead based his position on personal opinion; for this he was dismissed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.
春秋逆王后于齊 uses 逆 in the classic bridal-reception sense go to meet the queen, not a hostile moved against.

Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's discussion that the empress does not use her surname, and that in Spring and Autumn the queen was moved against to Qi. Cheng did not cite classic evidence clearly but established the discussion by personal opinion; on this account he was removed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.

Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's discussion that the empress does not use her surname, and that in Spring and Autumn the queen was met and escorted from Qi. Cheng did not cite classic evidence clearly but established the discussion by personal opinion; on this account he was removed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.
The literal repeats the false military reading of 逆王后于齊; met and escorted from Qi matches the Spring and Autumn usage.
Zhou was called the old statutes; Han spoke of precedents. From the He and Luo down to the Huai and sea, the court's laws and measures always looked to prior standards.
The Zhou spoke of old statutes; the Han spoke of precedents. From the He and Luo down to the Huai and sea, the court's laws and measures always looked to prior standards.
周稱舊章 means Zhou invoked or spoke of the old statutes, parallel to 漢言故事; was called the old statutes misreads 稱.

Huan Mi did not hurry to the imperial tombs; Left Assistant Zheng Xi did not impeach Mi but impeached Imperial Censor Kong Xin directly, also stating that he separately took charge of Orchid Terrace inspection—this is what is meant by impeaching the Imperial Censor directly.

Huan Mi did not hurry to the imperial tombs; Left Assistant Zheng Xi did not impeach Mi but impeached Imperial Censor Kong Xinshi directly, also stating that he separately took charge of Orchid Terrace inspection—this is what is meant by impeaching the Imperial Censor directly.
The personal name is the three-character 孔欣時. Kong Xin drops 時; Kong Xinshi is complete.

Huan Mi did not hurry to the imperial tombs; Left Assistant Zheng Xi did not impeach Mi but impeached Imperial Censor Kong Xin directly. It also said he separately took charge of Orchid Terrace inspection—this is what is meant by impeaching the Imperial Censor directly.

Huan Mi did not hurry to the imperial tombs; Left Assistant Zheng Xi did not impeach Mi but impeached Imperial Censor Kong Xinshi directly. It also said he separately took charge of Orchid Terrace inspection—this is what is meant by impeaching the Imperial Censor directly.
The literal likewise truncates 孔欣時 to Kong Xin; Kong Xinshi restores 時.
Mi's impeachment came after the present niche; the matter proceeded under sagely illumination.
Mi's impeachment came after the present accession; the matter proceeded under sagely illumination.
今龕 is not a physical niche. In this memorial it marks the present dynastic settlement, so present accession matches 今龕之後 and the idiomatic present reign.
Imperial Censor Zhang Yong was bound and dismissed.
Imperial Censor Zhang Yong was accordingly dismissed.
結免 is the case concluded in dismissal, not physical binding. Accordingly dismissed restores the legal sense of 結.
Imperial Censor Zhang Yong was bound and removed.
Imperial Censor Zhang Yong was accordingly removed from office.
The literal bound and removed similarly mistakes 結 for binding with ropes; 結免 is consequential removal from office.
The following year he was transferred to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Officials.
The following year he was transferred to Supervising Attendant and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Personnel.
給事中 is Supervising Attendant, not Attendant Within the Yellow Gates (黃門侍郎). Ministry of Personnel is an accurate rendering of 吏部.
The next year he was transferred to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Officials.
The next year he was transferred to Supervising Attendant and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Personnel.
The literal likewise equates 給事中 with the Yellow Gates office; Supervising Attendant is the correct title.
He was transferred to Regular Attendant at the Palace Library, Director of the Palace Library, Rectifier of Wu Commandery, and Grandee for the Palace.
He was transferred to Regular Attendant, Director of the Palace Library, Rectifier of Wu Commandery, and Grandee for the Palace.
The Chinese lists 散騎常侍 and 祕書監 as two posts. Regular Attendant at the Palace Library fuses them; the repaired list keeps them distinct.
He was transferred to Regular Attendant at the Palace Library, Director of the Palace Library, Rectifier of Wu Commandery, and Grandee for the Palace.
He was transferred to Regular Attendant, Director of the Palace Library, Rectifier of Wu Commandery, and Grandee for the Palace.
The literal has the same fusion of 散騎常侍 with 祕書監; they are separate offices.
He was additionally made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, retaining his post as rectifier.
He was additionally made Attendant for Affairs, retaining his post as rectifier.
加給事中 is not the Yellow Gates post. Attendant for Affairs is an accurate English title for 給事中.
He was additionally made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, with his rectifier post as before.
He was additionally made Attendant for Affairs, with his rectifier post as before.
The literal repeats the Yellow Gates mistranslation of 給事中; Attendant for Affairs is correct.
Cheng met Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Wang Daolong on the road and kowtowed until it bled; on this account he was pardoned.
Cheng met Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Wang Daolong on the road and kowtowed until it bled; on this account Xian was pardoned.
鮮…當死 is the topic of 見原. Cheng kowtows; Xian, not Cheng, is the one pardoned. The idiomatic field already names Xian.

Zheng Xuan was born at the end of Han; his teaching was ample and harmonious, the Confucian school of an entire age. Bao and Cheng walked the same path; elders regarded him as a former exemplar, and the young did not dare dissent.

Zheng Xuan was born at the end of Han; his teaching was ample and harmonious, the Confucian school of an entire age, running on the same track as Baocheng; elders regarded him as a former exemplar, and the young did not dare dissent.
褒成 is one compound, not Bao and Cheng, but the proposal makes Baocheng the walker of 竝軌. The teaching is the subject: it ran on the same track as the Baocheng tradition.
